_meta.indication: IXEMPRA in combination with capecitabine is indicated for the treatment of patients with metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer resistant to an anthracycline and a taxane (or taxane-resistant with anthracycline contraindicated), and as monotherapy for metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer in patients whose tumors are resistant or refractory to anthracyclines, taxanes, and capecitabine

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized trial comparing ixabepilone plus capecitabine to capecitabine alone; patients randomized 1:1
pivotal_trials.population: Adult women with metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer previously treated with an anthracycline and a taxane and resistant to such therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) by Independent Radiologic Review
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 5.7 months (IXEMPRA+capecitabine) vs 4.1 months (capecitabine); Hazard Ratio 0.69 (95% CI 0.58-0.83); p<0.0001. Objective tumor response rate 34.7% vs 14.3%.

nct_ctgov.title: Novel Epothilone Plus Capecitabine Versus Capecitabine Alone in Patients With Advanced Breast Cancer

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, multicenter study of ixabepilone monotherapy 40 mg/m2 every 3 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Women with metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer whose tumors recurred or progressed following an anthracycline, a taxane, and capecitabine
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response rate (ORR) by Independent Radiology Review Committee
pivotal_trials.result: Objective tumor response rate 12.4% (95% CI 6.9-19.9) by IRR assessment (n=113); all responders had a partial response, no complete responses

nct_ctgov.title: Novel Epothilone (BMS-247550) in Patients With Metastatic Breast Cancer (MBC)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) include peripheral sensory neuropathy, fatigue/asthenia, myalgia/arthralgia, alopecia, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis/mucositis, diarrhea, and musculoskeletal pain. Grade 4 neutropenia occurred in 36% (combination) and 23% (monotherapy); grade 3/4 peripheral neuropathy in 23% (Study 046) and 14% (Study 081).
target_moa: Ixabepilone is a semi-synthetic analog of epothilone B that binds directly to beta-tubulin subunits on microtubules, suppressing microtubule dynamics and leading to cell cycle arrest in mitosis and cell death
modality: Small molecule (semisynthetic epothilone B analog, microtubule inhibitor)

boxed_warning.content: Toxicity in hepatic impairment: IXEMPRA in combination with capecitabine must not be given to patients with AST or ALT >2.5 x ULN or bilirubin >1 x ULN due to increased risk of toxicity and neutropenia-related death

basis.text: Application carried a Priority (P) review designation

summary.text: Ixabepilone (Ixempra), a new molecular entity, received regular (full) approval under a Priority review designation for metastatic/locally advanced breast cancer; the application was not referred to ODAC, with the combination indication based on the primary PFS endpoint of randomized Phase 3 trial CA163046 and the monotherapy indication based on ORR from single-arm trial CA163081.

citations.quote: The reviewers recommend on the basis of this review of NDA 22-065 that ixabepilone (Ixempra™) receive regular approval for the following indications:
This application was not taken to a meeting of the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) because, for the following reasons, we determined the application did not warrant ODAC review.
